messages:
maya: Hey folks, just noticed my health insurance card shows start date 2026-04-01 but my hire date is 2026-03-29. I have a prescription from today. Is there a way to get covered or file a retro reimbursement? cc @lisa :thinking:
benefits-bot: Enrollment received. Coverage effective date: 2026-04-01. Retro coverage depends on carrier policy. Please submit receipts to Expensify with category `healthcare-reimbursements`. See: https://redwood.intranet/benefits/reimbursements :link:
lisa: Hi Maya 97 sorry for the confusion. Our standard carrier effective date is the 1st of the month following enrollment. Because your service date is before the effective date, it won't be automatically covered. However, we can request a retro review from the carrier. Please attach the itemized receipt and pharmacy printout, and include the prescription name and NPI of the prescriber.
maya: Thanks. For Expensify, should I mark the expense as pre-tax or post-tax? Also should I include the pharmacy copay amount only or full charge?
tom-payroll: Mark it as `healthcare-reimbursements` and in the description note `new-hire retro request`. For amounts: upload the full charged amount and attach the copay breakdown if available. If the carrier approves retroactive coverage, we will process the reimbursement non-taxably. If they deny and we reimburse as a discretionary payment, payroll will advise on tax handling.
olivia: Small FYI: If anyone else is in the same boat, we sometimes get faster responses by opening a People Ops ticket and adding "benefits: urgent medical" in the subject. That gets routed to our benefits admin queue.
maya: Uploading docs to Expensify now. One last thing 97 any special redaction rules for pharmacy receipts (they include Rx numbers)?
lisa: Please redact full credit card numbers and full SSNs. Rx numbers are fine to include unless they contain patient identifiers; you can blur them if you prefer. Keep patient name and date of birth.
maya: Submitted. Expensify report ID ER-8342, attached receipt + prescriber note. Also opened People Ops ticket #PO-4019. Thanks everyone! :pray:
benefits-bot: Ticket PO-4019 logged. Benefits admin will review within 3 business days. If carrier needs additional info, an agent will reach out.
olivia: Quick note on timing: if approved, reimbursements are issued as a separate vendor payment and may take one additional payroll cycle to appear. If you need the meds urgently, let us know and we can discuss short-term advance options.
maya: Not urgent, thanks. Appreciate the help! :smile:
